lehigh-2015-02.title: Equations
lehigh-2015-02.body:
Let the original have $S$ ounces of syrup and $W$ of water: $S=\frac13(S+W)$, so $W=2S$. After adding $6$ ounces of water the syrup is $20\%=\frac15$ of the total: $5S=W+6+S$, so $4S=W+6=2S+6$, $S=3$, $W=6$.

Total original liquid: $9$ ounces.

**Answer: 9**

lehigh-2015-03.title: Equal times
lehigh-2015-03.body:
With $x$ questions, Sam needs $4x$ minutes and Dave needs $x+60$ minutes. Setting them equal: $4x=x+60$, so $x=20$.

**Answer: 20**

lehigh-2015-04.title: Compare circumferences
lehigh-2015-04.body:
In equal times, the distances run are in the ratio of the speeds, $2:1$, so the smaller track has half the circumference $120\pi$, i.e. $60\pi$.

The radii are $60$ and $30$ meters, so the tracks are $30$ meters apart.

**Answer: 30**

lehigh-2015-05.title: Proportions
lehigh-2015-05.body:
The parts are $2k,4k,6k$ with $12k=64$, so $k=\frac{16}3$ and the shortest part is $2k=\frac{32}3$.

**Answer: 32/3**

lehigh-2015-06.title: Right triangle
lehigh-2015-06.body:
The broken top part is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $36$ and $27$ (a $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle scaled by $9$), so it has length $45$.

The pole's height was $36+45=81$ feet.

**Answer: 81**

lehigh-2015-07.title: Use symmetry
lehigh-2015-07.body:
The $8$ vertices are equivalent by symmetry, so the region closer to $v$ than to the other vertices is one of $8$ congruent pieces (the small cubes of side $2$ obtained by cutting the cube through its center). Hence $S$ has $\frac18$ of the volume that is inside the cube and outside the sphere.

That volume is $4^3-\frac43\pi\cdot2^3=64-\frac{32}3\pi$, and $\frac18$ of it is $8-\frac43\pi$.

**Answer: $8-\dfrac{4\pi}3$**

lehigh-2015-10.title: Weights
lehigh-2015-10.body:
The probabilities are $\frac j{21}$ since $1+2+\dots+6=21$. An even number: $\frac{2+4+6}{21}=\frac{12}{21}=\frac47$.

**Answer: 4/7**

lehigh-2015-11.title: Intersect
lehigh-2015-11.body:
$x^2+x=3x+4\iff x^2-2x-4=0$, so $x=1\pm\sqrt5$. The $x$-coordinates differ by $2\sqrt5$. Both points lie on a line of slope $3$, so the $y$-coordinates differ by $6\sqrt5$.

Distance $=\sqrt{(2\sqrt5)^2+(6\sqrt5)^2}=\sqrt{20+180}=\sqrt{200}=10\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $10\sqrt2$**

lehigh-2015-12.title: Angle chase
lehigh-2015-12.body:
Let $\angle ACB=x$. Since $CD=AD$, $\angle CAD=x$ and $\angle ADB=2x$ (exterior angle). Since $AB=AD$, $\angle ABD=\angle ADB=2x$. Since $CA=CB$, $\angle ABC=\angle CAB=2x$ as well, and the angle sum in triangle $ABC$: $x+2x+2x=180^\circ$, so $x=36^\circ$.

**Answer: 36**

lehigh-2015-14.title: Corners and edge squares
lehigh-2015-14.body:
Let the corner sum be $c$ and the edge-square sum $m$ (the four middle squares of the sides). The four sides each contain two corners and one edge square, so $2c+m=4\cdot42=168$ while $c+m=111$. Hence $c=57$, $m=54$.

Let the two integers be $p>q$ and $d=p-q$. If $a$ corners and $b$ edge squares equal $p$: $4q+ad=57$ and $4q+bd=54$, so $(a-b)d=3$, i.e. $d=1$ or $d=3$.
- $d=1$: $4q=57-a$ forces $57-a$ divisible by $4$, so $a=1$; but then $a-b=3$ needs $b=-2$. Impossible.
- $d=3$: $a=b+1$ and $4q=57-3a$ is divisible by $4$ only for $a=3$: $q=12$, $p=15$, $b=2$.

This works: corners $15,15,15,12$ in order around the square, with side-middle entries $12,12,15,15$: every side sums to $42$.

**Answer: 12 and 15**

lehigh-2015-15.title: Telescoping product
lehigh-2015-15.body:
Using $\log_b c=\frac{\ln c}{\ln b}$, the product telescopes: $f(n)=\frac{\ln n}{\ln 2}=\log_2n$. So $f(2^k)=k$ and
$$\sum_{k=2}^{99}k=\frac{99\cdot100}2-1=4949.$$

**Answer: 4949**

lehigh-2015-16.title: Median minimizes the sum
lehigh-2015-16.body:
The sum of distances to three points is minimized at their median. The points are $a<10<a+10$ (since $0<a<10$), so the median is $10$ and
$$f(10)=(10-a)+0+a=10.$$

The minimum value is $10$, independent of $a$.

**Answer: 10**

lehigh-2015-17.title: Count the disjoint subsets
lehigh-2015-17.body:
$A$ has $2^{26}$ subsets and $\frac18$ of them are disjoint from $B$, i.e. $2^{23}$ subsets. The subsets disjoint from $B$ are exactly the subsets of $A\setminus B$, which has $2^{26-|B|}$ of them. So $26-|B|=23$ and $|B|=3$.

**Answer: 3**

lehigh-2015-19.title: Center $(h,r)$
lehigh-2015-19.body:
A circle tangent to the $x$-axis (above it, since both points have positive $y$) has center $(h,r)$ and radius $r$. Passing through the points:
$$(h-1)^2+(r-9)^2=r^2,\qquad(h-8)^2+(r-8)^2=r^2.$$
Subtract: $14h-2r-46=0$, so $r=7h-23$. Substituting into the first equation: $h^2-128h+496=0$, so $h=4$ or $h=124$, giving $r=5$ or $r=845$.

Check: $(4,5)$: distance to $(1,9)$ is $5$; to $(8,8)$ is $5$. $(124,845)$: distance to $(1,9)$ is $\sqrt{123^2+836^2}=845$.

**Answer: $5$ and $845$**

lehigh-2015-20.title: Simplify to a double angle
lehigh-2015-20.body:
The denominator is $2+\cot^2\theta+\tan^2\theta=(\cot\theta+\tan\theta)^2$ since $\cot\theta\tan\theta=1$. And $\cot^2\theta-\tan^2\theta=(\cot\theta-\tan\theta)(\cot\theta+\tan\theta)$. The ratio is
$$\frac{\cot\theta-\tan\theta}{\cot\theta+\tan\theta}=\frac{\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta}=\cos2\theta.$$
For $\theta=15^\circ$: $\cos30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}2$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt3}2$**

lehigh-2015-21.title: Times per side
lehigh-2015-21.body:
Let $x,y,z$ be the hours for the three sides. The first $\frac34$ of the distance is the first two sides plus $\frac14$ of the third: $x+y+\frac z4=\frac72$. The last $\frac34$ is the last two sides plus $\frac14$ of the first: $\frac x4+y+z=\frac92$. The middle third of the distance is the second side, the first third is the first side: $y=x+\frac16$.

Substitute $y$: $2x+\frac z4=\frac{10}3$ and $\frac54x+z=\frac{13}3$. From the first, $z=\frac{40}3-8x$; into the second: $\frac54x+\frac{40}3-8x=\frac{13}3$, so $\frac{27}4x=9$, $x=\frac43$. Then $y=\frac32$, $z=\frac83$.

Total: $\frac43+\frac32+\frac83=\frac{11}2$ hours.

**Answer: 11/2**

lehigh-2015-22.title: Write $x=n+f$
lehigh-2015-22.body:
Let $x=n+f$ with $n=[x]$ and $0\le f<1$. Then $x^2=n^2+2nf+f^2$, so $[x^2]-n^2=[2nf+f^2]$, and we need $2015\le 2nf+f^2<2016$.

Since $f<1$, $2nf+f^2<2n+1$. We need $2n+1>2015$, so $n\ge1008$ ($n=1007$ gives $2nf+f^2<2015$ for all $f<1$). For $n=1008$: $2016f+f^2$ ranges continuously from $0$ up to nearly $2017$, so it takes values in $[2015,2016)$ (e.g. $f=0.9995$). So $n=1008$ works.

**Answer: 1008**

lehigh-2015-24.title: Generating function
lehigh-2015-24.body:
For $|r|<1$, $\sum_{n\ge1}n^2r^{n-1}=\frac{1+r}{(1-r)^3}$. With $r=\frac13$: $\frac{4/3}{8/27}=\frac{9}2$.

(Derivation: $\sum_{n\ge0}r^n=\frac1{1-r}$; differentiating gives $\sum nr^{n-1}=\frac1{(1-r)^2}$; multiplying by $r$ and differentiating again gives $\sum n^2r^{n-1}=\frac{1+r}{(1-r)^3}$.)

**Answer: 9/2**

lehigh-2015-25.title: Factor
lehigh-2015-25.body:
$\frac1x+\frac1y=\frac14\iff4(x+y)=xy\iff(x-4)(y-4)=16$ with $x,y\neq0$.

$16$ factors as $uv$ with $u=x-4$, $v=y-4$: $u\in\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm4,\pm8,\pm16\}$, giving $10$ pairs $(u,16/u)$. The pair $u=v=-4$ gives $x=y=0$, which is not allowed. So $9$ pairs remain.

**Answer: 9**

lehigh-2015-26.title: Roots $s-d,\ s,\ s+d$
lehigh-2015-26.body:
Write the roots as $s-d,s,s+d$. The sum of roots is $3s=3$, so $s=1$. The product is $s(s^2-d^2)=-6$, so $1-d^2=-6$ and $d^2=7$. Then $b=$ (sum of pairwise products) $=3s^2-d^2=3-7=-4$.

The roots are $1,\ 1\pm\sqrt7$; the smallest is $1-\sqrt7$.

**Answer: $(-4,\,1-\sqrt7)$**

lehigh-2015-27.title: Differences
lehigh-2015-27.body:
A common prime divisor $p$ divides the differences $193499-180253=13246=2\cdot6623$ and $180253-160921=19332=4\cdot4833$, so $p\mid6623$ or $p=2$; and $p$ divides $6623-4833=1790=2\cdot5\cdot179$.

The three numbers are odd and do not end in $0$ or $5$, so $p=179$. Indeed $193499=23\cdot47\cdot179$, $180253=19\cdot53\cdot179$, $160921=29\cdot31\cdot179$.

**Answer: 179**

lehigh-2015-28.title: Coordinates
lehigh-2015-28.body:
Put the circle's center at the origin and the chords on the lines $x=a$ and $y=a$ ($a>0$), by symmetry. The chord $x=a$ has half-length $\sqrt{1-a^2}$ and runs from $y=-\sqrt{1-a^2}$ to $\sqrt{1-a^2}$; it meets $y=a$ at height $a$. The two segments have lengths $\sqrt{1-a^2}-a$ and $\sqrt{1-a^2}+a$ in ratio $1:4$:
$$4\left(\sqrt{1-a^2}-a\right)=\sqrt{1-a^2}+a\ \Rightarrow\ 3\sqrt{1-a^2}=5a\ \Rightarrow\ 9(1-a^2)=25a^2\ \Rightarrow\ a^2=\frac9{34}.$$

The chord length is $2\sqrt{1-\frac9{34}}=2\sqrt{\frac{25}{34}}=\frac{10}{\sqrt{34}}=\frac{5\sqrt{34}}{17}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{34}}=\dfrac{5\sqrt{34}}{17}$**

lehigh-2015-29.title: Powers of 3 in the denominators
lehigh-2015-29.body:
Split the terms by their $3$-adic valuation. The terms with $27\mid i$ are $i=27,54,\dots,162$ ($i=27j$, $j=1,\dots,6$) and give $\frac1{27}\left(1+\frac12+\dots+\frac16\right)=\frac1{27}\cdot\frac{49}{20}$. The numerator $49$ and denominator $20$ are not divisible by $3$.

The other terms have denominators with at most $9=3^2$ exactly dividing, so their sum has the form $\frac A{9B}$ with $3\nmid B$ ($A$ an integer). Hence the total is $\frac A{9B}+\frac{49}{27\cdot20}=\frac{3A\cdot20+49B}{27\cdot20B}$ (common denominator $27\cdot20B$). The numerator $60A+49B$ is not divisible by $3$ since $3\nmid49B$. So the reduced denominator has exactly $3^3$ in it.

(A direct computation with exact fractions confirms $n=3$.)

**Answer: 3**

lehigh-2015-30.title: Signed distances are additive
lehigh-2015-30.body:
Take the line as the $x$-axis. Then the signed distances are $y$-coordinates. Since $D=A+C-B$ for a parallelogram, $y_D=y_A+y_C-y_B$. Here $y_A=\pm1$, $y_B=\pm2$, $y_C=\pm5$ with independent signs. WLOG $y_A=1$ (reflect the picture), so
$$y_D=1+(\pm5)-(\pm2)\in\{8,\,4,\,-2,\,-6\}.$$
Distances: $8,4,2,6$.

**Answer: $2,4,6,8$**

lehigh-2015-31.title: Mod 2
lehigh-2015-31.body:
Modulo $2$, $(x+1)^{2^k}\equiv x^{2^k}+1$. Write $2000=1024+512+256+128+64+16$ (binary $11111010000$, six ones). Then
$$(x+1)^{2000}\equiv(x^{1024}+1)(x^{512}+1)(x^{256}+1)(x^{128}+1)(x^{64}+1)(x^{16}+1),$$
which expands to $2^6$ distinct monomials (all exponents differ since they come from distinct subset sums of powers of $2$), each with coefficient $1$.

So $64$ coefficients are odd.

**Answer: 64**

lehigh-2015-32.title: Count move types
lehigh-2015-32.body:
To go from corner to corner we need a net displacement $(4,4)$. If there are $D$ diagonal, $H$ horizontal and $V$ vertical moves, then $D+H+V=6$ and $D+H=4$, $D+V=4$. Subtracting: $H=V$ and $D=4-H$, so $4-H+2H=6$ gives $H=2$, $D=2$, $V=2$.

Arrange the letters $DDHHVV$ in order: $\frac{6!}{2!\,2!\,2!}=90$.

**Answer: 90**

lehigh-2015-33.title: Find the angle
lehigh-2015-33.body:
When the right end is at $x=4$, the left end is at $(1,0)$ (angle $0$). The left end makes $240$ revolutions per minute $=4$ per second, so after $\frac{91}3$ seconds it has made $\frac{364}3=121\frac13$ revolutions, i.e. it is $\frac13$ revolution ($120^\circ$) past the start: $\left(-\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)$.

The right end is $(x,0)$ with $x>0$ at distance $3$: $\left(x+\frac12\right)^2+\frac34=9$, so $\left(x+\frac12\right)^2=\frac{33}4$, $x=\frac{-1+\sqrt{33}}2$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{33}}2$**

lehigh-2015-34.title: Rationalize
lehigh-2015-34.body:
The expression requires $1+2x\ge0$, i.e. $x\ge-\frac12$, and $x\ne0$ (to avoid a zero denominator). Since $(1-\sqrt{1+2x})(1+\sqrt{1+2x})=1-(1+2x)=-2x$, we get $\frac{2x}{1-\sqrt{1+2x}}=-(1+\sqrt{1+2x})$, hence
$$\frac{4x^2}{(1-\sqrt{1+2x})^2}=(1+\sqrt{1+2x})^2.$$
Expanding $(1+\sqrt{1+2x})^2=2+2x+2\sqrt{1+2x}$, the inequality becomes
$$2+2x+2\sqrt{1+2x}<2x+9\iff\sqrt{1+2x}<\frac72\iff1+2x<\frac{49}4\iff x<\frac{45}8.$$

Combining with the domain: $-\frac12\le x<\frac{45}8$, $x\ne0$.

**Answer: $\left[-\frac12,0\right)\cup\left(0,\frac{45}8\right)$**

lehigh-2015-35.title: Parity and mod 3, mod 5
lehigh-2015-35.body:
Let $a\le b\le c$. If all three are odd, then $a^4+b^4+c^4-3$ is even and larger than $2$, so it is not prime. If two or more are $2$: $2,2,2$ gives $45$ and $2,2,c$ with $c$ odd gives $c^4+29$, even and $>2$. So exactly one is $2$: $a=2$ and $b,c$ are odd primes, $p=b^4+c^4+13$.

Mod $3$: for $b,c\ne3$, $b^4\equiv c^4\equiv1$, so $p\equiv1+1+13\equiv0$, composite. Hence $b=3$ (the case $b=c=3$ gives $175$, composite): $p=c^4+94$ with $c\ge5$.

Mod $5$: for $c\ne5$, $c^4\equiv1$ and $p\equiv1+94\equiv0$, composite. So $c=5$ and $p=625+94=719$, which is prime (not divisible by $2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23$ and $27^2>719$).

**Answer: 719**

lehigh-2015-36.title: Count pairs of vertices
lehigh-2015-36.body:
Two vertices are joined either by an edge, by a diagonal inside a face, or by an interior diagonal. So $I=\binom V2-E-P$, where $P$ is the number of face diagonals.

Let $F_n$ be the number of $n$-gon faces. Then $2E=\sum nF_n$ and Euler's formula $V-E+F=2$ gives, for $V=13$, $22=\sum(n-2)F_n$. Face diagonals: $P=\sum\frac{n(n-3)}2F_n$. Then
$$I=78-\sum\left(\frac n2+\frac{n(n-3)}2\right)F_n=78-\sum\frac{n(n-2)}2F_n .$$
Under the constraint $\sum(n-2)F_n=22$, we want to minimize $\sum\frac n2(n-2)F_n$; since $\frac n2\ge\frac32$ with equality only for triangles, the minimum is $\frac32\cdot22=33$ when all faces are triangles ($F_3=22$, $E=33$, no face diagonals).

So $I_{\max}=78-33=45$. This is realized by a triangulated polyhedron, e.g. two pyramids on a common $11$-gon.

**Answer: 45**

lehigh-2015-37.title: Affine map to an equilateral triangle
lehigh-2015-37.body:
Affine maps preserve ratios of areas and map ellipses to ellipses. Map the $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle to an equilateral triangle; by symmetry the maximal inscribed ellipse in the equilateral triangle is its incircle, so the maximal ellipse in any triangle (the Steiner inellipse) has area ratio equal to
$$\frac{\text{incircle}}{\text{triangle}}=\frac{\pi(s\sqrt3/6)^2}{s^2\sqrt3/4}=\frac{\pi\sqrt3}9 .$$
The $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle has area $6$, so the answer is $6\cdot\frac{\pi\sqrt3}9=\frac{2\pi\sqrt3}3=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt3}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi\sqrt3}3$**

lehigh-2015-38.title: Menelaus
lehigh-2015-38.body:
Let $AG=x$, $GH=y$, $HM=z$.

Apply Menelaus' theorem to triangle $ABM$ with transversal $C$-$H$-$E$ (line $CE$ meets $AM$ at $H$, $AB$ at $E$, and $BM$ extended at $C$): $\frac{AH}{HM}\cdot\frac{MC}{CB}\cdot\frac{BE}{EA}=1$, i.e. $\frac{x+y}z\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac13=1$, so $x+y=6z$.

For transversal $C$-$G$-$D$: $\frac{AG}{GM}\cdot\frac{MC}{CB}\cdot\frac{BD}{DA}=1$, i.e. $\frac x{y+z}\cdot\frac12\cdot3=1$, so $x=\frac23(y+z)$.

With $z=1$: $x+y=6$ and $3x=2y+2$, giving $x=\frac{14}5$, $y=\frac{16}5$. So $AG:GH:HM=\frac{14}5:\frac{16}5:1=14:16:5$.

**Answer: 14:16:5**

lehigh-2015-39.title: Count tails-ending strings
lehigh-2015-39.body:
Let $a_n$ be the number of length-$n$ strings with no run of $3$ heads. A valid string ends in $T$, $TH$ or $THH$ (preceded by a valid string of length $n-1$, $n-2$, $n-3$ respectively), giving $a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}+a_{n-3}$ with $a_0=1$, $a_1=2$, $a_2=4$:

$a_3=7,\ a_4=13,\ a_5=24,\ a_6=44,\ a_7=81,\ a_8=149,\ a_9=274,\ a_{10}=504$.

$P(n)=1-\frac{a_n}{2^n}$: $P(9)=1-\frac{274}{512}\approx0.465<\frac12$ and $P(10)=1-\frac{504}{1024}\approx0.508\ge\frac12$.

**Answer: 10**

lehigh-2015-40.title: Law of cosines
lehigh-2015-40.body:
The crease $XY$ ($X$ on $AB$, $Y$ on $AC$) is the perpendicular bisector of $AD$, so $XD=XA$ and $YD=YA$. Let $AY=a$ so $YD=a$ and $CY=12-a$, with $CD=9$ and $\angle C=60^\circ$. Law of cosines in $CYD$:
$$a^2=81+(12-a)^2-9(12-a)\ \Rightarrow\ a^2=81+144-24a+a^2-108+9a\ \Rightarrow\ 15a=117,\ a=\frac{117}{15}=\frac{39}5.$$
Similarly with $AX=b=XD$, $BX=12-b$, $BD=3$: $b^2=9+(12-b)^2-3(12-b)$, so $21b=117$, $b=\frac{39}7$.

In triangle $AXY$ with $\angle A=60^\circ$: $XY^2=a^2+b^2-ab=39^2\left(\frac1{25}+\frac1{49}-\frac1{35}\right)=39^2\cdot\frac{49+25-35}{1225}=\frac{39^3}{1225}$.

So $XY=\frac{39\sqrt{39}}{35}\approx6.96$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{39\sqrt{39}}{35}$**
